articles.title: Your Family Lives There. So Why Is New York Imposing a Pied-à-Terre Tax?
articles.narrative: This opinion piece argues that New York City's pied-à-terre tax is being inadvertently applied to primary residents due to common real estate ownership structures like trusts and LLCs. The author contends that the tax, intended for absentee owners of high-value residential property, is unfairly burdening families who have a member living in the apartment full-time. The article highlights how the tax rules fail to 'look through' these entities to recognize the primary resident, leading to unintended tax liabilities and potential disputes among beneficiaries. The author urges the New York City Department of Finance to clarify its guidance to align with the law's original intent and suggests interim strategies for owners to restructure their holdings to qualify for exemptions.

articles.title: Power Availability Defining Most Coveted Locations in CRE
articles.narrative: A new report from the Urban Land Institute (ULI) and Heitman highlights that power availability and robust broadband connections are becoming critical determinants of commercial real estate value and investment, driven by the surge in demand for artificial intelligence. The report projects global data center investment to reach $7.6 trillion by 2030, with $3 trillion directly tied to real estate. Markets capable of quickly producing new power sources and leveraging existing grid infrastructure will gain a competitive advantage, with industrial facilities, pre-approved powered land, and battery storage properties also poised to benefit. The authors emphasize that real estate values will increasingly be shaped by power availability, proximity to users, and technological readiness, influencing property design and requiring resilient power sources for automation and robotics in industrial assets.

articles.title: Get to Know the Broker: Patrick Southern of Serhant
articles.narrative: This article profiles Patrick Southern, a residential broker at Serhant, highlighting his significant transaction volume in New Jersey, particularly Jersey City. Southern aims to elevate Jersey City's residential market to rival Manhattan's luxury appeal. He recounts his career's largest deal, managing the sale of a 700-property portfolio for a hedge fund, and discusses his current goal of building a new development business in New Jersey with Ryan Serhant.

articles.title: Scarcity, Privacy and Authenticity Are Luxury Development’s Calling Cards Now
articles.narrative: This opinion piece argues that the definition of luxury in residential real estate has shifted from quantifiable metrics like square footage and amenity counts to experiential qualities such as privacy, authenticity, craftsmanship, and a genuine sense of place. The author, a developer, emphasizes that discerning buyers are increasingly seeking homes that respond thoughtfully to their neighborhood's history and character, rather than following generic formulas. Key supporting points include the importance of natural materials, durable construction, integrated outdoor spaces, and bespoke amenities that foster community and connection to the local environment. The author concludes that creating lasting value requires developers to invest in elements that ensure a building's longevity, functionality, and contextual relevance, even if these investments don't offer immediate marketing payoffs.

articles.title: Insurance Is Taking a Bigger Bite Out of Apartment Revenue
articles.narrative: Apartment insurance costs, after five years of increases, saw a modest 2.2% decline in 2025, according to CRED iQ's analysis. This relief, however, comes after a significant 28.5% jump in 2023, leaving current premiums more than double their 2019 levels. The Sun Belt markets, which experienced the sharpest increases, are now seeing the most significant rate reductions, with Florida, Texas, and Louisiana recording drops of 9.8%, 8.4%, and 10.5% respectively in 2025. Conversely, coastal apartment owners, particularly in California, continue to face rising premiums, with a 6.3% increase in California apartments in 2025. A key takeaway is that while the rate of increase has slowed, apartment revenue growth has not kept pace with the surge in insurance costs, leading to a larger portion of revenue being consumed by premiums.

articles.title: Sierra Ridge Capital Buys 123,032 SF Industrial Building in Phoenix for $31M
articles.narrative: Sierra Ridge Capital has acquired an industrial property located at 3137 East Elwood Street in Phoenix for $31 million. The 123,032-square-foot asset, built in 1995 and recently renovated, was fully leased to three tenants at the time of sale. Newmark represented the seller in this transaction.

articles.title: Cadence McShane breaks ground on Parkhill Middle School in Dallas
articles.narrative: Cadence McShane Construction Company has broken ground on the new Parkhill Middle School in Dallas, Texas, for the Richardson Independent School District. This three-story, 201,209-square-foot facility is part of a district-wide initiative to convert junior high schools into middle schools serving grades six through eight. The project includes extensive site improvements and is expected to be completed by December 2028.

data_points.notable_features: Features classrooms, collaborative learning spaces, administrative offices, a library, a cafeteria, competition gyms, and locker rooms. Site improvements include a track, practice field, tennis courts, and a courtyard plaza.
data_points.project_notes: Developed through a multi-phase construction program to maintain campus operations during construction. Part of RISD’s district-wide initiative to transform junior high schools into middle schools serving grades six through eight.

articles.title: Morgan celebrates opening of 345-unit apartment community in North Austin
articles.narrative: Morgan has announced the opening of The Watson, a new 345-unit apartment community in North Austin, TX. The seven-story, podium-style property offers studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom homes with high-end finishes and a wide array of amenities, including two pools, co-working spaces, and multiple sky terraces. The development is strategically located in North Austin's tech corridor, near The Domain and future public transit, with approximately 45 units designated for households earning up to 60% of the Area Median Income.

data_points.notable_features: Designed for NGBS Green Silver certification and pursuing Austin Energy Green Building 1-Star certification, with 10-foot ceilings, quartz countertops, and private sky terraces in select units. Features a skyline plunge pool overlooking The Domain and a sunset roof terrace.
data_points.project_notes: Approximately 45 residences are reserved for households earning up to 60% of the Austin Area Median Income. Includes 522 parking spaces with EV charging stations and Wi-Fi connectivity.

articles.title: IMPACT Strategies breaks ground on film, TV production campus in Wood River
articles.narrative: IMPACT Strategies has broken ground on Hollywood River Studios, a new film and television production campus in Wood River, Illinois. The project is anticipated to bring substantial economic investment and job creation to the Metro East region, featuring six state-of-the-art sound stages designed for diverse film and television productions.

articles.title: Now is the time to dream out loud: Expanded Negro Leagues Baseball Museum set to bring new life to Kansas City’s famed 18th & Vine Jazz District
articles.narrative: The Negro Leagues Baseball Museum is undertaking a $35 million expansion in Kansas City's 18th & Vine Jazz District, which will include a new 35,000-square-foot museum building and a 144-room Pennant Hotel by Marriott. The project aims to significantly increase exhibit space and provide ancillary event areas, with a target completion by 2029. This development is expected to revitalize the historic district, bringing increased commercial activity and celebrating the legacy of Black baseball, according to the museum's president.

data_points.property_name: Negro Leagues Baseball Museum Expansion / Pennant Hotel

data_points.project_notes: The Negro Leagues Baseball Museum owns the Paseo YMCA building, which has been transformed into the Buck O’Neil Education and Research Center. Construction is expected to break ground in Q1 2027 and take 18-24 months.

articles.title: RESTO Athletic establishes world headquarters RS Impact Exchange in Kansas City
articles.narrative: RESTO Athletic, an athletic apparel manufacturer, has leased the entire second floor of the historic RS Impact Exchange at 3110 Troost Avenue in Kansas City, MO, for its new world headquarters. This 8,189-square-foot lease represents a significant expansion for the company, which is relocating from a nearby facility. The RS Impact Exchange is a community-centered retail and social impact hub developed by the nonprofit Reconciliation Services, with all tenant lease proceeds reinvested into their client programs and the revitalization of the Troost corridor. The project, which includes a $1.3 million Jackson County investment for accessibility upgrades, is expected to open in early 2027.

data_points.notable_features: Historic Baker Shoe Building reimagined as a community-centered retail and social impact hub; 100% of tenant lease proceeds are reinvested into client programs and corridor revitalization.
data_points.project_notes: Jackson County funded $1.3 million for a new west entrance, ADA accessibility, and an elevator. Construction is underway on the second floor.

articles.title: Producer Prices Jump 1.3%, Largest Monthly Increase Since March 2022
articles.narrative: Wholesale prices experienced a significant surge in September, marking the largest monthly increase since March 2022, primarily driven by a sharp rise in energy costs. The Producer Price Index for final demand climbed 1.3% for the month, contributing to a 6.3% annual increase, the highest since December 2022. Goods prices, particularly energy and gasoline, were the main contributors to this inflationary trend, with services also seeing an increase.

articles.title: EQT to Acquire Stockbridge, Adding US$16.5B in AUM
articles.narrative: EQT AB has agreed to acquire Stockbridge, a U.S. real estate investment manager, for a base consideration of US$375 million, with an additional US$175 million potentially paid over four years. The acquisition, expected to close in Q1 2027, includes 100% of Stockbridge's management company and general partner entities, adding approximately US$16.5 billion in fee-generating assets under management to EQT's real estate platform. This strategic move aims to significantly expand EQT Real Estate's offerings, integrating Stockbridge's diversified strategies and alternative sectors as a dedicated business line, and combining its industrial capabilities with EQT's existing industrial platform.

data_points.project_notes: Additional US$175 million to be paid over four years, contingent on performance. Acquisition covers 100% of the Stockbridge management company and general partner entities.

articles.title: CMBS Special Servicing Rate Climbs to New Post-2013 High
articles.narrative: The CMBS special servicing rate increased by seven basis points in September to 11.49%, reaching its highest point since February 2013. This rise followed a more significant 33-basis-point increase in August. While the overall rate climbed, performance varied by property type, with retail, lodging, and multifamily seeing increases, while mixed-use, office, and industrial experienced declines. New transfers to special servicing totaled approximately $2.65 billion, with office properties representing the majority of these transfers.

articles.title: AI Spurs Unprecedented Proptech Interest, Along with Questions (VIDEO)
articles.narrative: The emergence of artificial intelligence has ignited unprecedented interest in proptech, drawing more real estate companies to technology conferences than ever before, according to Michael Beckerman, CEO of CREtech. Despite this heightened engagement, there is significant uncertainty within the industry regarding the optimal path for AI adoption, with companies weighing whether to implement off-the-shelf solutions, develop proprietary tools using platforms like Claude or Gemini, or pursue a hybrid approach. This discussion highlights the current state of proptech investment and the long-term implications of AI for commercial real estate firms and their workforce.

articles.title: Space Race: How The Private Sector's Orbital Aspirations Are Driving CRE On Earth
articles.narrative: The surge in private sector investment into space exploration and development is directly fueling a significant expansion in production-oriented real estate. This trend indicates a growing demand for specialized facilities on Earth to support orbital aspirations, suggesting a new frontier for commercial real estate driven by technological advancement and private capital.

articles.title: Russell Galbut Axes 3 Miami Beach Live Local Act Projects
articles.narrative: Developer Russell Galbut has canceled three proposed Miami Beach projects that sought to utilize Florida's Live Local Act to bypass local zoning regulations. The decision follows significant community opposition to the high-rise developments, which aimed to bring new housing to the area. The Live Local Act, designed to encourage affordable housing, has faced challenges in implementation when it conflicts with established local zoning and community preferences.

articles.narrative: A foreclosure lawsuit has been filed against the stalled Penn Plaza life sciences project, which was planned as a 156,000-square-foot lab and office building. The project, developed by Cannon Hill Capital Partners, failed to advance beyond its initial planning stages.

data_points.project_notes: Planned as a lab and office building that never took off.

articles.title: Regulators Reject Proposed Rules For Data Centers On Nation's Largest Grid
articles.narrative: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) has rejected PJM's proposal for data centers to provide their own capacity, introducing uncertainty for the nation's largest grid system. This decision comes as the PJM grid has been experiencing significant strain, and the proposed rules aimed to address the growing energy demands of data centers within its operational footprint.
